The Letter

Context Internship, Semester 5Type LLM-driven game

The Letter was the name of the project I worked on for my internship in Semester 5. It’s a game using an LLM where the player takes on the task of being a mediator between people who have issues communicating effectively. The game focuses on the situation where two people have their own way of communicating, creating a “double barrier” that hinders communication.

The player has to analyze the way a person speaks in order to “construct or deconstruct” a message. In the deconstruct phase the player has to analyze text and get to the core of the message, removing all the extra fluff from it. In the construct phase the player has to do the opposite. This is done through a card-based puzzle.

The game aims to bring awareness to this issue, and to look at whether it can be used to improve communication in real-life situations, with the use of different scenarios.

The goal of the internship was to connect The Letter to a currently relevant social problem, on a subject being researched by other parts of the Lectoraat. This was done by using a scenario tailored to that specific problem.

Castle Bookdale

Context Game Production SemesterType Educational adventure gamePitched at Dragon’s Den, Spring 2026

Castle Bookdale is an educational adventure game in which children with language problems, such as dyslexic children and refugees, explore a magical castle, play minigames and learn about language. Along the way, they learn more about language, and practice and grow more confident in their skills.

I collaborated with experts on the matter, which helped massively in making this project a success. The combination of my expertise in creating a digital product and their expertise in language problems in children and teaching in general meant the game wasn’t just good on its own, but also fitted the needs of its target audience.

I presented our project in person at Dragon’s Den, Spring 2026, where we pitched the product to a panel of industry experts, the so-called Dragons. It was an informative afternoon, and as a group we were able to turn a lot of valuable feedback into improvements.

Future Frame

Context Dutch Design Week 2026Client Moral City HuntType Interactive installation

Future Frame was an installation for Dutch Design Week 2026. The aim was to collect data on the public’s assumptions and visions regarding a future with drones. The research team of Moral City Hunt, the client, assumes that XR technology is the most effective way to create an immersive experience for this goal. To prove or disprove that assumption, an A/B test is done with XR and non-XR technology.

For this installation, the rest of the team and I made an experience in which users “look into the future” through a portal, using parallax head-tracking technology. Users then move from side to side to choose which version of the future they want. Through dynamic changes in the environment and a video on a second screen, the consequences of their choices become apparent.
